learning_outcomes.text: Interpret key aspects of the economic and business context, from a strategic perspective.
Understand and analyze the main relationships between the main economic and business variables.
Know and integrate essential notions of business organization and management.
Identify and know the functions performed by the different subsystems of the company (financial, productive, commercial, and management and administration).

Understand and apply multi-criteria analysis techniques for decision-making in the financial, productive, and commercial fields of the company. This includes: Calculate and evaluate the main indicators of the economic and financial management results of the company. Identify the main existing sources of financing and explain their distinctive characteristics. Analyze and evaluate different investment alternatives. Identify different production strategies. Identify the main instruments and techniques of the commercial management of the company and their practical application.

syllabus_topics: Module I.- THE COMPANY AND ITS ENVIRONMENT
Module II.- THE FUNCTIONAL SUBSYSTEMS OF THE COMPANY.
6. THE PRODUCTION FUNCTION IN THE COMPANY
6.1 Concept and elements of the business production system
6.2 Objectives and decisions of the production system
6.3 'Just In Time' and new flexible and lean production systems
7.1 Design of the Business Production Plan
7.2 Main strategic decisions of the production system
7.3 Main tactical and operational decisions of the production system

Activities to be developed in English (reading and analysis of a current article or practical case, resolution of practical exercises, viewing of an explanatory video of a business management process or model, or attendance at a seminar)
assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, students must complete three tests: two during the semester, each weighing 25%, and a final one on the official exam date, weighing 50%. The convocation is considered used if the student takes the third continuous assessment test or activities that sum to at least 51% of continuous evaluation. For single evaluation, students take a single exam consisting of a theoretical part (50%) and a practical part (50%). Students can opt for single evaluation by notifying via the virtual classroom before continuous evaluation activities reach 40% weighting. In the second convocation, grades from continuous evaluation are not carried over.
